parts:
Hey everyone,

I'm calculating a large distance matrix using the dist() function
(~10000 x-y coordinates). I'd like to perform a function on each row
(or column) of this matrix which outputs a data.frame. Thus, I use
adply() to achieve this. The problem is that I need to convert the
dist object to an array using as.matrix(). This step is horribly
memory-intensive and it is the bottleneck of my program. Is there a
way to use the dist object as a regular matrix object on the fly
without having to convert it beforehand? A simple version of my code
is below.

> a<-data.frame(b=1:5,c=c(3,4,5,2,7))
> a
b c
1 1 3
2 2 4
3 3 5
4 4 2
5 5 7
> d<-dist(a,diag=T,upper=T)
> d
1 2 3 4 5
1 0.000000 1.414214 2.828427 3.162278 5.656854
2 1.414214 0.000000 1.414214 2.828427 4.242641
3 2.828427 1.414214 0.000000 3.162278 2.828427
4 3.162278 2.828427 3.162278 0.000000 5.099020
5 5.656854 4.242641 2.828427 5.099020 0.000000
> d2<-as.matrix(d)
> d2
1 2 3 4 5
1 0.000000 1.414214 2.828427 3.162278 5.656854
2 1.414214 0.000000 1.414214 2.828427 4.242641
3 2.828427 1.414214 0.000000 3.162278 2.828427
4 3.162278 2.828427 3.162278 0.000000 5.099020
5 5.656854 4.242641 2.828427 5.099020 0.000000
> sumd<-adply(d2,1,sum)
> sumd
Var1 V1
1 1 13.061773
2 2 9.899495
3 3 10.233345
4 4 14.252002
5 5 17.826942
> d4<-adply(d,1,sum)
Error in splitter_a(.data, .margins) : Invalid margin

In the case of a large number of coordinates in the data.frame a, the
d2<-as.matrix(d) step takes forever or hangs, while the actual dist
calculation takes only a few seconds. Using adply on the dist object
does not work. If anyone has any tips on this, that would be great.
Thank you.

Faisal Moledina

You may think that d is a matrix but it is really a vector that is the
lower triangular elements in column-wise order. I did come up with an
alternate but it is not any faster.

> system.time(replicate(1000, {dn <- diag(0,5,5);
+ dn[lower.tri(dn)] <- d;
+ dn[upper.tri(dn)] <- d} )
+ )
user system elapsed
0.087 0.000 0.087

> system.time(replicate(1000, {dn <- as.matrix(d)} ))
user system elapsed
0.055 0.001 0.059

Looking at as.matrix.dist you can see that 4 matrices of equal equal
size to d (row(df), col(df), t(df), df) must be created for conversion
of a dist object to a matrix object:
getAnywhere(as.matrix.dist)

function (x, ...)
{
size <- attr(x, "Size")
df <- matrix(0, size, size)
df[row(df) > col(df)] <- x
df <- df + t(df)
labels <- attr(x, "Labels")
dimnames(df) <- if (is.null(labels))
list(1L:size, 1L:size)
else list(labels, labels)
df
}

Perhaps the above will help in understanding why you are running into
space limitations. The code on stack overflow provides a method after
suitable augmentation of the d vector to c(0, d) for indexing the
array elements without creating extra matrices, but does not appear to
solve the speed problem, but perhaps it will keep you from getting
your process from overflowing into virtual memory:

system.time(replicate(1000, {dn <- matrix( c(0,d)[1+sapply(1:5,
function(i) noeq.1(i, 1:5, 5))], 5,5) } ))
user system elapsed
0.512 0.003 0.525
